correctness.rationale: A complete support-functional classification reduces every Birkhoff-orthogonal unit pair, up to dihedral symmetry, to a facet-endpoint family or a vertex with a kernel direction between the coordinate and diagonal rays. The endpoint family gives the exact candidate envelope and a fixed pair attains it for every lambda. In the interior case, Birkhoff orthogonality, the first-coordinate bound u>=1/sqrt2, and a norming functional for y give the three lower bounds 1, sqrt2-1+lambda/sqrt2, and lambda-(sqrt2-1). This proves the exact denominator profile. Piecewise logarithmic derivatives then show that the generalized rectangular quotient can maximize only at lambda=2(sqrt2-1) or lambda=2sqrt2, yielding the stated maximum of two branches.
risks: The checker is finite and supplementary; the universal lambda and p quantifiers rely on the analytic proof.
The theorem does not assert a closed-form crossing exponent between the two branches.

originality.rationale: The defining modern full text was inspected at the definition of mu_p, its regular-hexagon calculation, and its final ell_p estimates; exact searches for octagon and octagonal returned no occurrence. The later paper with the potentially confusable title Generalized rectangular constant in Banach spaces was obtained in full and inspected: it recalls mu_p only as background and introduces different constants mu(X,a) and mu prime(X,a). published-finding corpus searches covered the invariant name, regular-octagon aliases, the candidate two-branch formula, and the denominator-profile formulation. The closest same-invariant public hit is mu_4 on ell_4^2, while the own ledger contains only the p=1 octagonal endpoint.

value.rationale: The generalized rectangular family was introduced precisely to track how Birkhoff-orthogonal distortion changes with the exponent. The regular hexagon is the canonical polygonal example in the defining source, so the next highly symmetric polygon is a motivated benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice. The result is structurally stronger than a one-number computation: the exact denominator profile d_8(lambda) isolates three geometric regimes and shows that the all-p constant is governed by competition between two intrinsic Birkhoff scales. It recovers the known ordinary rectangular endpoint, produces the nontrivial p-to-infinity limit 4-2sqrt2, and supplies a reusable support-functional template for other polygonal norms.
risks: The result is a canonical exact-family benchmark, not a classification of generalized rectangular constants for all regular polygons.
